title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude Code self-hosted environments — public-beta runners execute sessions inside your own network
bullets.summary: Anthropic's public beta (v2.1.224) lets Team/Enterprise orgs run `claude self-hosted-runner` on their own machines/containers; sessions started from claude.ai, mobile, desktop, or `claude --cloud` then execute inside your network with internal-service access, in fixed or on-demand pools, each session isolated to its own repo checkout.
bullets.how: The compute model The Construct needs: Hermes's credentialed jobs (DreamHost SSH, GSC, GitHub) must run on Bobby's own Mac/network — self-hosted runners keep Cowork/Claude Code work inside that trust boundary with per-session isolation instead of Anthropic's cloud.

bullets.title: Claude for Government — Claude Code + Cowork now public beta in a FedRAMP-High Gov Desktop with tamper-evident audit logs
bullets.summary: The agentic file-work stack ships to public-sector teams with stronger admin controls, tamper-evident audit logs, and spend governance; Anthropic stays the contracted/billing party so agencies need no separate cloud relationship.
bullets.how: Proof the exact bundle PRAGMA sells — agentic execution + tamper-evident audit trail + spend governance — is what regulated buyers pay a premium for; a positioning template for the governed-operator pitch and an eventual public-sector lane for B9/PRAGMA.

bullets.title: arXiv counter-signal — orchestration is not free; for procedural tasks a well-prompted single agent can beat a swarm
bullets.summary: The paper documents orchestration's reliability costs (cascading errors, routing failures, poor cross-trial consistency — 60% pass@1 yielding only ~25% consistency across trials) and shows in-context prompting matching or obsoleting multi-agent orchestration on procedural work.
bullets.how: A corrective to the 'orchestration is the moat' read: reserve multi-agent orchestration for heterogeneous, high-value jobs, collapse simple procedural steps into one well-prompted agent, and measure cross-trial consistency (not just pass@1) before promising a client an SLA.

bullets.title: Getty Images ships an MCP server — licensed creative, editorial, and archival visuals now agent-callable
bullets.summary: Announced Aug 12, the Getty MCP server gives agents a standardized way to discover, retrieve, and license Getty's creative/news/sport/entertainment/archival library inside AI workflows and products.
bullets.how: A rights-clean image source B9 agents can pull for mockups, headers, and social without licensing risk, and the cleanest template yet for the PRAGMA pitch — a client's own DAM exposed as one governed MCP server the operator agent calls.

bullets.title: xAI ships Grok 4.6 (Aug 12) plus Grok Imagine Image 2.0 (Aug 8) — another frontier tier + image engine in one week
bullets.summary: Grok 4.6 lands as xAI's newest frontier model and Grok Imagine Image 2.0 as a fresh text-to-image engine, days apart.
bullets.how: Bench Grok 4.6 as a routing option for reasoning/computer-use jobs and Grok Imagine 2.0 against Higgsfield for B9 creative; keep model routing abstract so we can swap the best-of-week engine under the sub-agents.

praxis_lesson: The afternoon's fresh signal sharpens the moat thesis: it isn't just 'orchestration' in the abstract — it's running agents inside the client's own trust boundary (self-hosted Claude Code runners on owned compute) with a tamper-evident, spend-governed audit trail (the Claude-for-Government bundle). That is precisely PRAGMA's sellable edge. The arXiv counter-signal is the discipline check — don't over-orchestrate; match architecture to task, collapse procedural work into one well-prompted agent, and measure cross-trial consistency before promising an SLA.
